messages:
sana: Ran a focused nsys + perfetto trace against the dedicated pool (flash-attn fused variant + KV write hot path). Seeing sustained DRAM write bandwidth spikes coincident with 'flash_attn_fused_kv_write' NVTX ranges — I think write IO is saturating the copy path for batches > 24. Posting timeline + quick dumps.

jamie: Can you paste the nsys command and a small flame/snippet?

sana: Ran: `nsys profile --sample=cpu --trace=nvtx,cuda -o /tmp/attn_kv_write` then exported perfetto protobuf. Key snippet from the timeline: 
```
Range: flash_attn_fused_kv_write  | wall 450ms | sm_util 78% | dram_bw 110GB/s | memcpy_htod 120ms (burst)
Range: flash_attn_forward           | wall 220ms | sm_util 62% | dram_bw 40GB/s
CPU NVTX: kv_table_write() calls spike at same time as memcpy_htod bursts
```

mike: link to perfetto?

sana: uploaded: https://perfetto.google.cn/trace/abc123 (shortlink) — perfetto shows interleaved memcpy slices and the fused kernel executing; copy queues backpressure visible.

alex: hmm. If writes are serialized on a single stream while kernels run on another, we might be hitting H2D copy contention. Are we using pinned buffers for KV write?

sana: current path uses staging pinned buffers but we still see big memcpy bursts on long sequences. Also observed an nvprof metric: `dram_util` elevated during the fused-kv-write kernel vs fused-no-write variant (approx 2.6x).

jamie: did you try toggling kernel selector to prefer fused_no_write when write_ratio > 0.15? That should avoid the write-heavy kernel for many requests.

sana: I tried a quick selector patch: `if (avg_writes_per_batch / batch_size > 0.15) prefer fused_no_write` — bench on microbench harness:
```
workload: 128-token seq, batch 32, kv_write_ratio 0.2
before: p50=38ms p99=210ms throughput=420 tok/s
after:  p50=42ms p99=172ms throughput=390 tok/s
```
Result: p99 improved (less long tails) but throughput down ~7% on throughput-heavy steady state. Latency tail reduced because we avoided big H2D bursts.

mike: Tradeoff makes sense. We should bias selector using SLO class: latency-sensitive routes prefer lower p99 even if throughput drops a bit. Throughput-oriented routes keep fused_kv_write.

alex: Also file IO pattern: KV write aggregator flush currently does small frequent writes. Could batch KV commits async on a background copy stream and use stream priorities to deconflict. Perfetto shows copy slices interleaving with kernel warps. Might help to coalesce the writes into larger contiguous memcpy and push to high-priority stream during idle windows.

sana: Good idea. I prototyped coalescing: aggregate KV writes per-request-window and submit single H2D with `cudaMemcpyAsync` on stream 3. That reduced number of memcpy slices by ~6x and dropped dram_bw spikes. Microbench after coalesce + selector patch: 
```
workload same as above
combo: p50=40ms p99=150ms throughput=395 tok/s
```

jamie: Nice. Can you open a short RFC/PR with: 1) kernel selector heuristic, 2) coalesced KV-write path guarded by feature flag, 3) perfetto screenshots + nsys export? We'll canary on dedicated pool.

sana: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842 (WIP). Added NVTX zones for `kv_coalesce` and `kv_submit_stream` so traces are clearer.

perf-bot: Trace artifact uploaded: gs://redwood-inference/traces/2198723456/attn-kv-write-nsys.qdrep

mike: Plan: land PR behind runtime flag, run canary on 10% of dedicated pods for a day, gate on p99 latency and token/sec. If p99 improves without >5% throughput regression, promote.

sana: Will add telemetry: `kv_write_queue_depth`, `memcpy_burst_ms`, and `dram_bw_1s` to Console dashboard. Also adding an eval prompt set to track quality/regression for fused_no_write.

jamie: One more ask: please attach a short troubleshooting note in PR about how to reproduce nsys/perfetto steps and which perf counters to collect (sm_util, dram_bw, gld_throughput, gst_throughput).

sana: Will do. TL;DR: root cause = H2D copy bursts + synchronous write path in fused-kv variant -> mitigation = selector + coalesced async writes + NVTX for visibility.

mike: Thanks — solid investigative thread. Follow-up meeting if canary shows borderline regressions. :thumbsup:
